title: Recovery Run Positioning
content: A recovery run is a sprint made by an attacking player back toward their own goal when possession is lost, with the priority of getting goal-side of the ball as quickly as possible. The recovery runner's first objective is not to win the ball — it is to occupy a position between the ball and the goal, eliminating the direct route to goal for counter-attackers. Optimal recovery positioning: sprint toward the goal, then peel back to a position between the nearest attacker and the goal. The most common recovery error: sprinting laterally across the pitch instead of first getting goal-side. Two players in recovery should not chase the same attacker — one covers the ball carrier, the other covers the most dangerous runner ahead.
